intro: Cairo rewards visitors with pyramids, mosques, markets and Nile views. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: Metro: three lines, clean and cheap; tickets EGP8-20 by distance.
Buses: red-white-blue city buses EGP4-6; air-conditioned EGP7-12; minibuses EGP5-15.
Taxis: white cabs; meters often unused, agree or pay the fair sum on exit.
Ride apps: Uber and Careem work well in Cairo; often easier than street taxis.
Driving: not advised for visitors; traffic is heavy and rules are loose.
Walking: fine in some districts but crossings and pavements are poor; little cycling.

pyramids.name: Pyramids of Giza
pyramids.price_text: ≈ EGP 540 general site ticket; Great Pyramid interior extra — check on the day
pyramids.tip: Go at opening to beat heat and crowds, and ignore anyone offering unsolicited 'guides' or camel deals.

sphinx.name: Great Sphinx of Giza
sphinx.price_text: Included in the Giza plateau ticket
sphinx.hours: Same as the Giza plateau, roughly 08:00–17:00
sphinx.tip: The classic photo is from the viewing platform south-east of the Sphinx; go early for soft light.

egyptian-museum.name: Egyptian Museum
egyptian-museum.price_text: ≈ EGP 450 foreign adult — check on the day
egyptian-museum.tip: Many famous pieces have moved to the new Grand Egyptian Museum, so ask at the desk what is still here.

citadel.name: Cairo Citadel
citadel.price_text: ≈ EGP 450 site ticket — check on the day
citadel.tip: The Citadel walls give the best wide view over old Cairo; bring water, shade is limited.

muhammad-ali.name: Mosque of Muhammad Ali
muhammad-ali.hours: Daily roughly 08:00–17:00, closed to tourists at prayer times
muhammad-ali.tip: Dress modestly — cover shoulders and knees; shoes come off at the entrance.

khan-el-khalili.name: Khan el-Khalili
khan-el-khalili.price_text: Free to wander; pay for what you buy
khan-el-khalili.hours: Shops roughly 10:00–late evening; many closed on Friday morning
khan-el-khalili.tip: Bargain hard and start around half the asking price; the cafés off the main lane are calmer.

abdeen-palace.name: Abdeen Palace
abdeen-palace.tip: The palace museums are small and quiet; combine with a Downtown walk nearby.

al-azhar.name: Al-Azhar Mosque
al-azhar.tip: Women should carry a scarf; the courtyard is peaceful early in the day.

al-rifai.name: Al-Rifa'i Mosque
al-rifai.hours: Daily roughly 09:00–17:00, closed at prayer times
al-rifai.tip: Pair it with the Sultan Hassan Mosque across the street for one of Cairo's best architectural views.

bab-zuweila.name: Bab Zuweila
bab-zuweila.price_text: ≈ EGP 100 to climb the towers — check on the day
bab-zuweila.tip: Climb the minaret towers for a rooftop view over old Cairo; the stairs are steep and narrow.

babylon-fortress.name: Babylon Fortress
babylon-fortress.price_text: Free to see from outside; Coptic Museum covers the area
babylon-fortress.tip: Walk the old Roman walls between the Coptic churches in Coptic Cairo.

baron-empain.name: Baron Empain Palace
baron-empain.tip: The Hindu-inspired palace is a striking photo stop; the surrounding Heliopolis streets are worth a short walk.

bent-pyramid.name: Bent Pyramid
bent-pyramid.price_text: ≈ EGP 200 Dahshur site ticket — check on the day
bent-pyramid.tip: Far fewer crowds than Giza; you can sometimes enter the pyramid, ask at the gate.

stadium.name: Cairo International Stadium
stadium.price_text: Ticket prices vary by match — check on the day
stadium.hours: Only on match days or with a tour
stadium.tip: Only worth it if a big match is on; buy tickets through official channels, not touts.

cairo-land.name: Cairo Land
cairo-land.price_text: Pay per ride or a day pass — check on the day
cairo-land.tip: A family theme park; check opening days before travelling out.

opera-house.name: Cairo Opera House
opera-house.price_text: Ticket prices vary by performance — check the programme
opera-house.hours: Box office daytime; shows mostly evenings
opera-house.tip: Book ahead online for concerts; the riverside setting on Gezira is lovely at night.

cairo-tower.name: Cairo Tower
cairo-tower.tip: Go near sunset for the best view over the Nile and the city haze.

cave-church.name: Cave Church
cave-church.hours: Daily, daylight hours; services in the evening
cave-church.tip: Huge amphitheatre carved into the Mokattam hills; go with a local or taxi as it is in a busy area.

st-sergius.name: Church of St. Sergius and Bacchus
st-sergius.landmark: Church of St. Sergius and Bacchus
st-sergius.tip: One of the oldest churches in Cairo, said to shelter the Holy Family; dress modestly.

city-of-the-dead.name: City of the Dead
city-of-the-dead.price_text: Free to walk; go with a guide
city-of-the-dead.tip: A vast historic cemetery where people also live; visit respectfully with a local guide.

coptic-museum.name: Coptic Museum
coptic-museum.tip: Combine with the nearby churches and Babylon Fortress for a half-day in Coptic Cairo.

dream-park.name: Dream Park
dream-park.price_text: Pay per ride or day pass — check on the day
dream-park.tip: A large family amusement park near 6th of October; confirm it is open before a long taxi ride.

felucca.name: Nile felucca sail at sunset
felucca.price_text: ≈ EGP 300–600 per boat, agree the price first
felucca.hours: Best around sunset; boats run into the evening
felucca.tip: Agree the total price and duration before boarding, and confirm it is per boat not per person.

khan-food-walk.name: Old Cairo street food walk
khan-food-walk.price_text: ≈ EGP 150–300 for koshari, taameya and juice
khan-food-walk.tip: Eat where locals queue; koshari and taameya are cheap, filling and vegetarian-friendly.

zamalek-walk.name: Zamalek neighbourhood walk
zamalek-walk.hours: Any time; cafés and shops daytime to evening
zamalek-walk.tip: Leafy streets, galleries and cafés; a calm break from Downtown traffic.

muizz-tour.name: Al-Muizz Street guided walk
muizz-tour.price_text: ≈ EGP 400–800 per person with a guide — check on the day
muizz-tour.tip: A guide helps you find the small monuments along the street; agree the price and route first.

stays.why: Central for the Egyptian Museum, metro and cheap eats. Lively and noisy; good value.
Quiet island district with cafés and embassies. Calmer evenings, easy taxis to most sights.
Closest to the Pyramids and the Grand Egyptian Museum. Far from Downtown sights.
Near the airport and quiet streets. Best for early flights or a last night.

food: Try koshari: rice, lentils and pasta with tomato sauce. Cheap and filling, often under EGP 100.
Street snacks: ta'ameya (herb falafel), ful medames and fresh baladi bread. Look for busy stalls.
Grilled meats and pigeon are Cairo classics. Ask for the price before ordering at tourist-area restaurants.
Sweet tooth? Try basbousa and kunafa from a local sweet shop, sold by weight.
Tap water is not for visitors; drink bottled water and be careful with raw salads at cheap places.
more_time: Add a day for Islamic Cairo: the Citadel, Sultan Hassan Mosque and Khan el-Khalili bazaar.
Swap a city day for Saqqara and Dahshur to see older pyramids with fewer crowds.
Take a short Nile dinner cruise or a felucca ride at sunset instead of an evening indoors.
